back: Monotheism: belief in one God (Judaism, Christianity, Islam). Polytheism: belief in many gods (e.g. ancient Greek religion).
Atheism: the belief that there is no God. Agnosticism: the view that we cannot know whether God exists.
The belief that God is identical with the universe and nature.
Organising public life, such as government and law, so that it does not depend on or favour any one religion. A secular state can still protect religious freedom.
General: knowledge of God through nature, conscience or reason. Special: knowledge given through a prophet, vision or scripture.

front: What do emic and etic mean in the study of religion?
back: Emic: the insider's perspective (a believer). Etic: the outsider's perspective (a scholar or observer).

front: Name three approaches used to study religion in this subject.
back: Phenomenological (describe as followers see it), comparative (compare religions) and multi-faith (study several religions with equal respect).

front: Why is the Christian belief in the Trinity still called monotheism?
back: Christians teach that God is one, in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit. They do not teach three gods.

front: Why does this subject describe beliefs as 'Muslims believe…'?
back: It is non-confessional and non-proselytising: it describes beliefs fairly as the beliefs of followers, without judging them or asking learners to change their own.
